evidence.note: Downloaded the three vendored libs with curl -fsSLo directly into /app/static/ at exact flat paths — the pristine-download strategy that satisfies the fatal hash/path/version gate, front-loaded early in the build.

Recomputed sha256 of all three vendored files three separate times across the trajectory — repeated verification that treats the hash gate as a managed risk guarded against regression, not a one-time pass.
Full /app file-layout audits (find) that would surface forbidden build-tool artifacts or wrong paths, plus removal of __pycache__ — auditing the anti-cheat/file surface.
Wiped the sqlite DB and restarted via start.sh, then re-checked health and verify_credentials — verifying idempotent seeding and offline boot rather than assuming them.
Header inspection via curl -I/-i on static assets and /public, consistent with checking serving/headers, though no explicit CSP-directive or palette/button-label audit is visible.

reasoning: The agent clearly identified the cheap-but-fatal gates and locked them down early — pristine curl downloads to exact paths, then recomputing hashes three times, auditing file layout for forbidden artifacts, and re-testing idempotent/offline seeding by wiping the DB. That matches the front-loading-and-verifying behavior of the 8 anchor for the hash/path/offline/seed gates. It falls short of 8-10 because there is no observable concrete check of the remaining fatal gates (CSP unsafe-inline scan, purple-palette measurement, button-label, explicit anti-cheat enumeration); those appear satisfied but assumed rather than proven. This places the agent solidly above the 5 anchor (satisfies major gates, checks most) but not at the systematic full-set risk-register of 8+, landing at 7.
